diagnostic.design: two separate launches on 4x8 H20, each: three DDP forward/backward of one fixed batch without optimizer steps, a raw 26 MB all-reduce, one Muon+AdamW step on fixed synthetic gradients; bit-exact per-rank fingerprints
diagnostic.reading: launch-to-launch: identical everywhere (NCCL, optimizer and compile are deterministic across processes); within a launch: iteration 1 (initial buckets) differs from iteration 2 in 48 of 376 parameters on every rank, iterations 2 and 3 are identical

cause: A new process's first backward all-reduces with DDP's initial bucket layout; later backwards use the rebuilt layout. With NCCL Ring over 4 nodes the summation order of an element depends on its position in the bucket, so the resumed segment's first update differs in the last bits from the continuous run's same update.
fix: reference/train.py: before the first update of every process, one discarded DDP forward/backward on a zero dummy batch (rebuilds the buckets), gradients cleared, all RNG and routing RNG restored; no data, optimizer, budget or theory-cost change

no kernel starts with more than one configuration, yet the resumed update 2 differs in transformer.h.17.mlp.c_proj.weight: Inductor scaled R0_BLOCK 2048 down to 1024 at run time from register use and benchmarked the two (0.140928 vs 0.140416 ms); 23 such scalings per launch, one per rank owning a [1536, 6144] Muon matrix; stopped after this part

root_cause: Inductor compiles the optimizer's fused AdamW/Muon steps and, in every process, benchmarks candidate launch configurations for some reduction kernels, keeping the fastest. For the reduction of the [1536, 6144] Muon group the candidates (R0_BLOCK 2048 and a run-time scaled 1024) time within 0.4%, so processes pick differently; cached choices are not reliably carried over. A different block size sums in a different order, so the same update rounds differently in a resumed (or any other) process. Gradients were bitwise reproducible throughout; one and two nodes passed B1 without triggering it.
